broken_claims: THESIS/TITLE 'three monuments to people who thought they'd last' / 'three symbols of this will last forever' — false for 2:259 (no owner, no arrogance, no permanence theme; it is a resurrection lesson). The unifying anti-flex banner fits only 18:42 and 22:45.
'The Quran has ONE phrase / one image for ruin' framing invites a cherry-pick rebuttal: the bare word خاوية appears 5x incl. 27:52 (another ruin-for-wrongdoing verse) and 69:7.
required_corrections: 1) Do NOT sell all three under a single 'false permanence / they thought they'd last' theme — that fits 18:42 (18:35 'I do not think this will ever perish') and 22:45 (destroyed while wrongdoing) but NOT 2:259, whose town has no owner and no arrogance and whose lesson is resurrection. Present the shared PHRASE/IMAGE as the unifying thread and let the three lessons differ (as the exhibit itself states). 2) Preempt cherry-pick: state up front that the bare word khawiya appears 5x, but the exact 3-word phrase with 'ala 'urushiha (fallen onto its roofs) is the specific recurring image unique to these 3 — acknowledge 27:52 (Thamud's houses 'fallen empty because they wronged') and 69:7 ('Ad like hollow palm-trunks). 3) In 18:42 the structure is a garden/vineyard; 'urush there reads as grape trellises, so 'a building whose roof caved in' is strained for that verse — describe the collapse-onto-supports image without over-literalizing 'roof.' 4) Avoid the being/having angle on 18:42 (already published in the Two Gardens article).
notes: Load-bearing exhibit PHRASE-5 is bulletproof: exact contiguous phrase خاوية على عروشها = exactly {2:259, 18:42, 22:45}, mushaf order, purely Quranic, no hadith. Verified by contiguous-substring, token-membership, possessive-form, and corpus morphology. Proposal SURVIVES on the facts. The failures are in the persona-facing FRAME, not the count: the 'monuments to false permanence' headline overreaches on 2:259, and the 'one image for ruin' language exposes a 5x-vs-3x cherry-pick that a hostile reader will catch (27:52 is a second ruin-for-wrongdoing verse). Corrected article — 'one exact phrase, one collapse-image, three ruins, three lessons' — is straightforwardly publishable and more honest.
